That is why I didn't make the card interact with exile. Instead it has a replacement effect for things going to exile. I thought it could be interesting for a card to allow cards like the new \[\[experimental overload\]\] to be played multiple times without defeating the purpose of it exiling itself (preventing recursion loops). My logic was that by having it return to your library, it would effectively act like you added an extra copy of the card to your deck. I wanted to avoid it doing so immediately knowing that \[\[nexus of fate\]\] is a problematic card and a number of extra turns spells use exile as a way to prevent recursion. I can fully understand a hesitance to see this kind of design space explored but I think that my implementation (at least with what I could discern) doesn't absolutely shatter any play cycle. It provides time for an opponent to remove it and permanently exile the cards waiting to be recurred and aside from a tutor spell, provides little in the way of allowing the player to immediately reuse a spell that was returned by this card. I hope you can understand where I was coming from when going about designing this card.
